Checks#

This page is for maintainers: how Booster is checked, and where its proof lives. Next: Next for what is not built yet.

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in MAINTAINING.md.

Checks: composer ci (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Development happens on Wayne State's GitLab; this repository is a release mirror. Changes land there first.

composer ci

runs composer validate --strict, PHPUnit, Pint, PHPStan (Pinstripe's raw preset, inlined; waynestate/pinstripe ships with Booster and supplies the preset the advisory scan uses), composer audit, the hop data check and the agent-ready check. Nothing needs PHP on the host:

docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"

contract/expectations.json says what Booster must detect, plan and change for each example app in examples/; tests/ContractTest.php enforces it with the real Rector, so a Rector release that changes a hop shows up in CI.

Proof#

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private site, proof.apps.wayne.edu/booster, behind a Wayne State employee sign-in. The Real output page shows Booster's own plan and dry-run output on each example app, and composer ci keeps it current.

Proven how: the first full run with the gate on took a Laravel 12 app from PHP 8.2 to 8.4 in two hops, each gated by the app's 197-test suite, and it is written up in research/booster-e2e-gate.md.

Status#

See CHANGELOG.md for what changed, OPEN_QUESTIONS.md for what stays open, and BEST_PRACTICES.md for the rules Booster follows.
